distractors: Done out of habit and without conscious thought, the way you take the same route home without ever deciding to.
Announced in advance to everybody it will affect, so that nobody has to learn about it from somewhere else. It is about the warning, not the thinking.

Agreed collectively before being carried out, with everyone who will be affected having had a chance to object first. What it describes is how many people signed up to the thing, not the quality of the thought behind it.

Carried out despite an explicit instruction not to, where the person doing it knew the rule perfectly well and went ahead regardless. The weight of the word would sit in the defiance, which is a claim about the instruction rather than about the care taken.

Repeated at regular intervals on a fixed cadence, so that everybody knows when the next one falls without having to ask. It describes the rhythm on which a thing happens rather than the state of mind of whoever set that rhythm up, and a badly chosen cadence is kept just as faithfully as a good one.
